entities.summary: Antonio Correr was a Roman Catholic cardinal who played a pivotal role in the Great Western Schism of the 14th century. Appointed cardinal by his uncle Pope Gregory XII, Correr worked to resolve the schism through his diplomatic efforts and theological expertise. As a key figure in the negotiations, Correr's influence helped shape the course of the schism and its aftermath. The outcome of the schism led to the establishment of the Conclave of Pisa, which ultimately led to the election of Pope Martin V. Correr's legacy as a mediator and theologian has endured, with his contributions to the schism remaining an important chapter in the history of the Catholic Church. Despite the significance of his role, Correr's life and legacy remain somewhat overshadowed by the larger events of the time, making him an intriguing figure for historians and scholars to explore.
